about.title: Cerritos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a preventable collision changes everything, and Cerritos families dealing with this kind of loss often have questions no one has prepared them for. Public crash records show that Cerritos sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, with reported crashes clustering on corridors like SR-91, Artesia Boulevard, South Street, and I-605, often on Friday evenings. Behind those numbers are real households now facing funeral costs, lost income, and an absence that can't be measured. California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death claim, and if none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. We provide a free legal review and can explain the options available to your family, without judgment and without pressure, while you focus on what matters most right now.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and moving to other dependents or heirs if none exist. We can confirm who has standing in your family's specific situation.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Window Applies
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity can require action much sooner. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on a claim.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Medical Bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. This is a separate civil matter from any criminal case that may also be pending.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Cerritos?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children generally have first priority to file. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim instead. We can review your family's circumstances and clarify who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to take legal action?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government agency, such as a public entity responsible for a road like South Street or I-605, may be involved, the deadline to act can be much shorter. It's best to speak with us as soon as you're able.

items.question: Does this cost anything?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover something for your family. You can take time to grieve without worrying about upfront legal costs.
